<!-- pr-reviewer: be650bb3402b2187e8885c2c4e520be106f9162d -->
**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

**What looks good**
- The sweep is conservative where it matters for the field. A level piece is solved in closed form at the clamped bearing (field_arc.rs `nearest_tau`/`dist`, with the column engine's `flat_tie`/`bull_tie`). A helical piece takes the minimum of real pose evaluations plus a 1e-12 margin, so the field can only sit at or above the true distance. It never shows removal the tool did not make, and `residual()` bounds the overshoot at half a sample step.
- Windows and prunes grow by the piece's sagitta (field) or bulge `sag + |dz|` (scan: gouge bin walk, ridge boxes, SegGrid ring prune). Past half a turn the scan takes the diameter instead. The chord-count budget is unchanged, so refusals match the old behaviour.
- No `unwrap/expect/panic` in the new modules. Non-finite tolerances fall back to 0.01, and degenerate arcs fall back to the lone chord. Provenance headers are present. Touched files stay under 400 lines (scan.rs is 364). `Fixes #413`, a `Changelog:` line and a decisions file are in the PR. No CHANGELOG.md edit, no deps, no build.rs, .github or scripts changes. The commit subject is conventional.
- The pinning tests fail on the old code and pass on the new. The bull-nose parity is tightened back to 1e-5.

**Local results (merged with current main, no conflicts)**
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-sim` (all 33 binaries) | all pass, including field_arc_sweep 5/5, scan_arc 2/2, stock_bull_nose 7/7, arc_sweep 5/5, stock_backend_parity 13/13, stock_sdf_cut 12/12, lib 62/62 |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |
Not re-run: app, motion and the release heavy lanes (the PR reports them green; the diff is sim-only).

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Questions / notes (not blocking)**
1. scan_arc.rs `dist_tri` (and the helical `dist_pt`) use a sampled search plus golden section. Its result is a real evaluation, so it is at or above the true distance. For the field that errs toward keeping material. For the gouge verdict it can under-read a gouge by a tiny amount if the 1-D minimum is not unimodal inside a piece. Pieces are at most a quarter turn, so this should be far below `tol`. The old inscribed chords under-read concave over-cuts by up to `tol/4`, so this is a strict improvement. A short note that gouge depth carries this search bound would help.
2. The scan's rest, flank and hidden-rest verdict numbers on arcs can move by up to `tol/4` (already flagged by the author). Cost was not benchmarked beyond suite times.
3. Interaction with #499 (fixture-law arc sagitta pad): none in code. #499 touches only `crates/sim/src/verify/*` and its own test. #483 touches only `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/*`. They are different laws on the same family of problem (chords inside arcs), and they can merge in either order. #499 pads fixture-clearance chords outward by the sagitta. #483 makes the stock engines read the true arc instead of padding. No shared helper changes.
4. The GUI view of stock and timing on arc-heavy jobs were not hand-checked, as the author said.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
